Describes the real feature: a guided one-question-at-a-time walkthrough that leads the reader to BUILD the argument from the page's certified text; keeps the reasoning accurate (won't affirm a rail-violating step); same pastoral/orthodoxy rails. voiceover: What if, instead of handing you the answer, it taught you to build the argument yourself? That's the new 'Teach me this' tutor — right beside Ask AI Tutor, on every essay and evidence card. It doesn't lecture. It asks one short question at a time, and walks with you — step by step — until you've reasoned the whole argument out. You're not memorizing a case. You're building it yourself. It teaches straight from the page in front of you — and the full argument stays there to reread as you go. And it keeps you honest: it won't let a wrong step slide, so what you build actually holds up when someone pushes back. Read the essay and you can recite the case. Work through this and you can make it — in your own words. The difference between reading an argument, and being able to make it. Try 'Teach me this.'
